author: Temminck & Schlegel, 1845
habitat: 낙엽활엽수림, 침엽수림, 혼효림 등 산림, 관목이 흩어진 풀숲

months.note: 4~5월에 걸쳐 오며, 산란기는 5~8월이고 대부분 6월에 알을 낳는다.

summary: 4~5월에 걸쳐 찾아오는 흔한 여름철새로 전국에 살며, 국외에서는 러시아, 극동 남부, 중국 남동부, 동남아시아, 일본에 분포한다. 밤에 활동하며 낙엽활엽수림, 침엽수림, 혼효림 같은 숲과 관목이 흩어진 풀숲에서 지내고, 낮에는 어두운 숲속이나 우거진 가지에 가지 방향으로 가슴을 바짝 붙이고 있어 좀처럼 눈에 띄지 않는다. 대개 홀로 지내며, 대부분 6월에 침엽수림이나 혼효림 안 풀숲 빈터에 둥지 없이 알 2개를 낳아 암수가 번갈아 품는다. 날면서 큰 입을 벌려 나방, 딱정벌레, 물매미, 벌, 메뚜기 같은 곤충을 잡아먹는다.

points.en: cryptic plumage mottled brown, black and grey

points.ko: 날 때 긴 날개와 긴 꼬리
points.en: long wings and long tail in flight

sexes.text: 암수 모두 몸 전체가 갈색·검은색·회색이 섞인 얼룩무늬이다.

art.subject: Grey Nightjar (Caprimulgus jotaka), adult male in summer, resting by day in Korean forest from May to August: whole plumage cryptically mottled and vermiculated grey, grey-brown and black with buff and rufous spots, so that it looks like bark or dead leaves; crown grey with dark central streaks; white patches on the throat; underparts finely barred grey-brown and buff; long wings and tail mottled and barred like the body, with white spots near the tips of the outer tail feathers. Bill tiny and black, with a huge gape and stiff bristles at its base; large dark eye; legs and feet very short, brownish.
art.pose: resting lengthwise along a branch by day, breast pressed flat against it
art.scene: Korean summer mixed forest: shady interior with a small grassy clearing; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view resting lengthwise along a branch: large flat head, large dark eye, tiny bill, cryptic mottled grey, brown and black plumage, white throat patches, long wings and tail lying along the branch
adult male, flight from below: long pointed wings with a white patch across the outer primaries, long tail with white spots near the outer tips, wide gape open to catch insects
adult female, flight from below: same shape and mottling, with smaller buff patches on the outer primaries and no white in the tail
art.build: Medium-sized, long-winged, long-tailed night bird, 27–32cm, about as long as a pigeon but much slimmer and flatter. Large flat head with large dark eyes and almost no visible neck. Bill tiny, but the gape is enormous, opening wide back towards the eyes. Legs very short with tiny feet, barely visible. Rests lengthwise along a branch or flat on the ground, body horizontal and pressed down. At rest the long pointed wings reach well down the tail but not to its tip. Tail long, slightly rounded. Flight buoyant and agile on long pointed wings; the male shows a white patch across the outer primaries.
avoid: Do not perch it crosswise on a twig like a songbird; it lies lengthwise along a branch or flat on the ground.
Do not draw a hooked or long bill, long legs or forward-facing owl-like eyes.
Do not paint bright rufous or boldly contrasting plumage; it is a muted grey, brown and black mottle.
Do not give the female white wing or tail patches; hers are small and buff, or absent in the tail.
